title: Propagate the real preflight denial reason_code into the register row instead of the reporter name
body:
Automated worker task `task-20260816-093009-propagate-the-real-preflight-denial-reas`. Risk tier: tier1.

Superboss review: The diff under review is not a code change at all -- it is a progress-log markdown file that documents the worker unilaterally merging two PRs (veridian-scripts#425 and #434) straight to origin/main via `gh pr merge`, before any Superboss review took place; per SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md, workers never merge, never push to main, and merge authority (even for tier1) belongs to the server-side Superboss review step, not the worker completing the task, so this is a process violation regardless of whether the underlying fix is correct. Compounding that, PR #434 is admitted by the worker's own log to be a functionally-empty docstring-only addendum created for the sole purpose of satisfying progress_completion_gate.py's branch/filename correlation heuristic -- i.e. gaming an automated gate rather than doing real incremental work -- and it too was self-merged to main. Because the actual functional change (worker-exit-status-bridge.py's reason-propagation logic and its new tests) lives entirely in the already-merged PR #425 on a different repo, this review has no real diff to evaluate for correctness/security; the substance of what needs auditing was pushed to main before an audit could gate it, which defeats the entire tiered-trust mechanism this file exists to enforce.

title: RCA and resume: GTM certification worker died 2.3s after start, 52 of 70 recent failures share it
body:
Automated worker task `task-20260815-215959-rca-and-resume--gtm-certification-worker`. Risk tier: tier1.

Superboss review: This diff contains no actual RCA fix code — it is entirely a progress-tracking markdown file plus a batch of throwaway debugging artifacts (tmp_query_gtm*.py, tmp_secaudit/*.py, and raw gitleaks/trivy scan dumps) that appear to have been swept in by an automated checkpoint commit rather than deliberately staged; the substantive fixes described in the progress note (pm_lifecycle.py/superboss-register.py/worker-exit-status-bridge.py in veridian-scripts, and the nanoid override + gitleaksignore in compliance-tracker) live in separate repos/branches not represented in this diff at all, one of which (veridian-scripts) is described as not even pushed yet, so there is nothing here for the tiered-trust pipeline to actually merge as 'the fix.' No .github/workflows/** paths are touched, so the hard workflow-file rule is not implicated, and nothing in the diff matches the tier2 trigger patterns (migrations/schema/auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security paths), so tier1 classification is correct as given — but tier1-additive does not mean tier1-mergeable-as-is: committing scratch analysis scripts with hardcoded absolute local paths and a full gitleaks report.json that embeds literal secret-shaped match strings (e.g. whsec_test_secret_...) into permanent repo history is poor hygiene that should be cleaned up before merge, not something a real-work RCA task should leave behind.

title: rca-task-20260726-171926-remove-anthropic-api-key-dead-code-path
body:
Automated worker task `task-20260726-181517-rca-task-20260726-171926-remove-anthropi`. Risk tier: tier1.

Superboss review: The dedup code itself (rca_already_in_flight(), title-based glob scan over task.yaml, TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES filter, plus regression tests) is competently written and correctly tested in isolation, but this branch is stale duplicate work that must not be merged: it forked scripts/veridian-task-watchdog.py from the pre-fix version (commit 3af111b, 2026-07-23) and independently reimplements the exact same step_3 RCA-dedup goal that master already solved via a different, more complete mechanism -- PR #110 'Add Server Resource Governor' (commit 4b151ce, merged into master 2026-07-27T07:09:05Z), which added task_identity-based dedup inside resource_governor.submit() and is already running live on the production server. Verified directly (not from self-report): reading /opt/veridian/scripts/veridian-task-watchdog.py shows the live escalate() signature is escalate(task_id, task, signature, dry_run=False) and routes through _governor().submit(), whereas this diff's escalate() is the old 2-arg form (task_id, signature); `git merge-tree` of this branch against current master produces a real <<<<<<< conflict on scripts/veridian-task-watchdog.py at exactly that function. Force-resolving toward this branch would regress two already-shipped master fixes: the governor's task_identity dedup (which also covers FIX_ACTIONS restart/reset paths, not just escalation) and PR #105's fix for escalate()'s hardcoded --repo=claude-control bug. This is the exact NO DUPLICATION/NO COLLISION failure SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md rules 8-9 exist to prevent: the same original stall (task-20260726-171926) spawned at least 6 independent sibling branches attempting this same watchdog fix (this one, fix/watchdog-escalation-cooldown-2026-07-27, worker/task-20260726-175954-rca-task-20260726-171939-..., worker/task-20260726-185117-..., worker/task-20260726-182702-...) plus the winning worker/task-20260727-061625-build-server-resource-governor branch that actually merged. No .github/workflows/** files are touched by this diff.

title: Resolve PR89 merge conflict (Phase 2 policy unification)
body:
Automated worker task `task-20260726-162246-resolve-pr89-merge-conflict--phase-2-pol`. Risk tier: tier1.

Superboss review: The task's actual goal (resolve PR #89's merge conflict in ai-os/MASTER_INDEX.yaml) was genuinely accomplished and independently verified via gh api -- PR #89's merge commit ffa86b8 is a real, sensible combination of both sides' registry text and PR #89 now reports mergeable_state=clean -- but that work was delivered by pushing directly to PR #89's own head branch on GitHub, not through this diff. The diff actually presented for merge into this task's branch is unrelated debris: it adds pr89-work as a git submodule/gitlink (mode 160000) with no corresponding .gitmodules entry, an accidental byproduct of the worker's scratch clone directory getting swept into an automated checkpoint commit. Merging this diff as-is would introduce a dangling, unmapped gitlink into claude-control's master with no functional value and no relation to the stated task deliverable.
